clue.text: Bob has meadow to' cross in Lincolnshire?

parts.note: a bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated S in old British money
a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
a ford is a place to cross a river; to ford is to cross

explanation.surface: Someone with a shilling has to cross a field somewhere in the Lincolnshire countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place-description: SLEAFORD is a market town in Lincolnshire, an English county, and the question mark admits the definition is only by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of this name lies in the eastern English county, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Bob meets friend with girl composer

parts.note: a bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated S in old British money
a chum is a friend
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A hairdo meets a pal and a young woman who writes music.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert ___ was a German Romantic composer, so he is an example.

parts.note: a spiritualist medium at a seance is said to produce a ghostly substance from the body

explanation.surface: A middling amount of production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' looks like an adjective, average, but it is a spiritualist who claims to emit a ghostly substance.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed spirit matter exuded by a seance psychic is what such a person produces.

definitions.meaning: open land, the countryside or a meadow
the side not batting in cricket, spread around the ground

explanation.surface: A national cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: Open land as in fields of the countryside; and the fielding side in cricket, an English bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Poor Dora carries cask from building

indicators.note: carries says the anagram holds the cask word within it
poor says the name Dora is in bad shape, its letters reworked

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: Unfortunate Dora lugs a barrel out of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' gives RODA from DORA, and 'carries' puts TUN inside it; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A round building, typically domed, is a type of structure.

clue.text: In a way, Young's beginning to show indifference

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: beginning says take only the opening letter of the word Young's

explanation.surface: In some way a young person's first act shows they couldn't care less.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of interest or concern is the meaning of both words: synonyms.

clue.text: For a number, a tip about raising food

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
V is the Roman numeral five
an end is a tip

indicators.note: raising, in a down clue, says the word for about is read upward, backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone gives a tip for a number, perhaps about rearing the livestock feed.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for fodder or provisions, so it is a synonym for something to eat.

parts.note: strain read as a tune or melody; the time is the speed at which a piece is played

explanation.surface: A period of stress and tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress, but here it is a musical strain, a melody, whose speed is its time.
explanation.definitionFit: The speed of a piece of music is its pace, the musical time of a tune.

clue.text: Pulled Ken out in getting-up time

indicators.note: in says the scrambled name sits inside the reversed time word
getting-up, in a down clue, says the time word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: a day is a time

indicators.note: out says the letters of Ken are put out of order

explanation.surface: Ken was dragged out of bed at rising time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting-up' turns DAY into YAD; 'out' turns KEN into NKE, and 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerked or tugged hard: a synonym for hauled.

definitions.meaning: baffles or beats, as a hard question does
the bowler aims at the wooden uprights behind the batsman

explanation.surface: Losses are what a cricketer aims at.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle is to beat someone; and the wicket of three upright sticks in cricket is what the bowler targets.

parts.note: a heated tot of spirits taken at ten o'clock at night, read as three words, names an old term for a southern African people

explanation.surface: A savage warrior warms himself with a spiced drink before bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as HOT TEN TOT, a hot tot at ten, the nightcap is split into three words; the whole names a people once (offensively) called barbarians by colonists.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, now offensive European name for the Khoikhoi people, whom colonists cast as uncivilised.

parts.note: O.S., outsize, before a word for a male person describes someone obviously great; the whole names the founder of the Ottoman line

explanation.surface: Plainly one of the Ottoman rulers deserves the title great.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, so an OS MAN is obviously great in size; Osman I founded the Ottoman dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The first ruler of the Ottoman state bore this name, and the dynasty took its name from him.

clue.text: Mechanical mount was in low spirits

definitions.meaning: a motorised bicycle is something you ride, a mount with an engine
to have sulked or brooded listlessly

explanation.surface: Someone sat gloomily on their little motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-powered motorcycle is ridden like a horse; and the verb means sulked or moped about dejectedly.

clue.text: Naval officer of the more unfeeling sort ?

definitions.meaning: the first lieutenant of a ship is known by this nickname
more numb, a comparative of numb, plus a word for a type or kind

explanation.surface: A ship's officer turns out to be rather cold-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the first word as NUMB-ER, more unfeeling, and the second as ONE, a sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Navy slang for a ship's first lieutenant; and, split, a more numb kind.

clue.text: A big drop in profit returned by associate

indicators.note: returned says the word for profit is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: gain means profit
ARA stands for Associate of the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: A firm's profits fall sharply when a partner gives them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns GAIN into NIAG; 'by' simply joins it to ARA.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfall on the US-Canada border is a famously large fall of water.

clue.text: About 500 ales and too much French — E. Thomas remembered that !

indicators.note: about says the ales word goes around the number

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500
trop is French for too much

explanation.surface: A poet recalls a time of plenty of beer and too much French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts ALES around D to give ADLES. Edward Thomas's poem begins 'Yes. I remember Adlestrop', the Gloucestershire village where his train stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet Edward Thomas's best-known poem recalls this village halt: 'Yes. I remember' it.

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so these letters wrap the word for trouble
arranged says the letters of was are put in a new order

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A fight was organised with no difficulty at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns WAS into SWA, and 'without' (outside) puts it around ADO. Sadowa (Königgrätz), 1866, was Prussia's decisive victory over Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1866 Prussian victory over Austria is known by this Bohemian village's name, an example of a battle.

clue.text: Game involves a leap or two

indicators.note: involves in the sense of entangles or twists together, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A sport that calls for a jump or two.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' is a link; LEAPORTWO, nine letters, rearranges to give the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball sport played by swimmers in a pool, so it is an example of a game.

indicators.note: about says the care word goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to mind is to care

indicators.note: rough says the letters of mesh are roughed up into another order

explanation.surface: Be careful with coarse netting material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns MESH into SHME, and 'about' puts CARE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, a type of cloth.

definitions.meaning: the essayist Charles Lamb wrote as Elia

explanation.surface: A lamb introduces itself to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamb is Charles Lamb, whose essays were signed Elia: his introduction 'Am Elia' runs together into a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female given name, and also 'am Elia', the essayist's pen-name after the verb.

parts.note: the right is the conservative wing in politics

explanation.surface: A political faction is correctly set up.
explanation.definitionFit: It means correctly, in the right way: a synonym.

clue.text: A bitter somehow goes to one's head

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of a bitter are rearranged in some fashion

explanation.surface: A pint of bitter beer makes a drinker tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to one's head' looks like drink making one drunk, but it describes a hat: the square cap worn by Catholic clergy sits on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A square clerical cap is worn on top, so it is something placed upon the wearer's crown.

definitions.meaning: an old word for a cheeky or worthless woman

explanation.surface: A woman inside some boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for a saucy girl; and luggage, packed in suitcases.

explanation.surface: Damn the drink!
explanation.definitionFit: A hard thump is a heavy punch; and old British slang for beer or ale.

clue.text: Stopping the others dividing grain, possibly

indicators.note: dividing says one piece splits the other by sitting inside it
possibly says the letters of grain may be rearranged

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Halting the remaining people as they sort through the corn, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' makes ARING from GRAIN, and 'dividing' puts REST inside it, after AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean halting or bringing to a stop: synonyms.

definitions.note: read as Montague's son, the young hero of the Verona tragedy

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
nil is zero, O

explanation.surface: A Montague has no money at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money, but it is Italy's capital city; the definition reads Montague's (son), Shakespeare's lover in Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young lover is the son of old Montague, so he is Montague's boy.

definitions.meaning: a bundle of twigs used for flogging, as in 'the rod'

explanation.surface: A tree is used for beating wrongdoers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale-barked tree, and its twigs bound for flogging: the cane of old schools.

parts.note: a boy's name that is also something grown, a kitchen herb

explanation.surface: A lad who is getting bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'boy' is a boy's name that is also a herb grown in pots and gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a male first name and a culinary herb that is cultivated.

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something nasty was involved in a gruesome killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' looks like an adjective, nasty, but it defines an animal: the primate is a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A Madagascan primate is an animal, so it is something of the beastly kind.

clue.text: A grave matter, as the master's way of speaking shows

parts.note: the head is the headmaster, so the master's is the head's
tone is a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A serious business, as the schoolmaster's voice makes plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A grave matter' sounds like a serious affair, but grave is the burial place: the slab is a stone over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorial stone set over a burial place is literally matter belonging to a tomb.

indicators.note: in says the frolic word sits inside the abbreviation for training

parts.note: PT is physical training
a romp is a frolic

explanation.surface: Raring to go, they enjoy a bit of fun at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick and on time, prepared to act: a synonym in the sense of immediate.

definitions.meaning: thoroughly cooked to crispness, as of a steak or toast

explanation.surface: Applause for a sharp, snappy performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooked right through, as a crisp roast is; and the congratulation said to someone who succeeds.
